object_description: compact single-roof volume with an L-shaped equipment addition marking the settlement boundary
geometry_property: aligned to the high-rise building boundary
solid base with timber roof and facades
design_condition: the compact volume moves towards the main street to free as much space as possible for a new break area, breaking with the orthogonality of the existing buildings and aligning to the building boundary towards the open landscape

positive: The compact structure approaches the main street to free space for a new break area and future expansion
The L-shaped addition of the outdoor equipment room marks the settlement boundary
This is further accentuated by a striking edge to the hard court behind
The building volume is organised compactly
A transparent ground floor mediates between outside and inside
A spacious gallery enables a direct connection from the foyer to the gym
The staircase is centrally located and accessed via a vestibule
The cloakroom area and gymnasiums are accessed via a well-sized, clear anteroom
The equipment rooms are organised lengthwise beside the cloakrooms
The workrooms are accessed via a central cloakroom area and illuminated on two sides
Typologically the building is based on agricultural single-roof courtyard buildings
This combines various functions under one roof with a comparably large footprint
The materialisation is chosen accordingly, with canopies protecting the facade elements
Inner surfaces appear raw and can be selectively refined or ornamentally designed
The outdoor concept plays with developed and undeveloped fields of different uses
The existing break area is to be lined with trees and its geometry strengthened
The new break area is designed with tree islands and various play and lounge areas
The interior room arrangements are convincing in terms of functionality
The compact volume and proposed constructions suggest rather low construction costs
The concept for environmental design is comprehensible and carefully justified
negative: Breaking with the existing orthogonal pattern seems alien
The forced formation of squares with the corresponding terrain seems alien in relation to the landscape
The choice of building typology as an addition to the existing complex is not convincing
The spatial situation in the kindergarten area is unsatisfactory in views, lighting and outdoor space
